skill.name: firecrawl-parse
skill.description: Parse local documents with Firecrawl and save clean markdown output. Supports PDF, Word, OpenDocument, RTF, spreadsheet, and HTML files.
skill.summary: Convert local documents into clean markdown files with Firecrawl.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick and path traversal alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting and a relative documentation link. I found one contextual risk: local documents may be uploaded to Firecrawl during parsing. No prompt injection or malicious override text was found.

remediation.issue: Local document contents may be sent to Firecrawl for parsing.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation step before parsing sensitive or private files.

remediation.issue: The skill does not clearly disclose third-party processing before use.
remediation.suggestion: Document what data is sent, where it is processed, and how Firecrawl credits are used.

static_findings.snippet: Efficiently extract and convert the contents of any local file—such as PDF, DOCX, DOC, ODT, RTF, XLS
- Use `scrape` instead when the source is a URL
Always save to `.firecrawl/` with `-o` — parsed docs can be hundreds of KB and blow up context if st
Then `head`, `grep`, `rg` etc., or incrementally read the file - don't load the whole thing at once.
| `-Q, --query <prompt>` | Ask a question about the parsed content |
- Quote paths with spaces: `firecrawl parse "./My Doc.pdf" -o .firecrawl/mydoc.md`.
- Check `.firecrawl/` before re-parsing the same file.

semantic_findings.title: Local Document Upload Requires Explicit Consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to parse local files with Firecrawl and references upload limits and credits. Sensitive document contents may leave the user machine without a clear consent step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill handles any local file and mentions upload size and paid credits. That strongly suggests external service processing, though the file does not spell out the transport path.

content.value_statement: Local files often need clean text before review, search, or summarization. This skill uses Firecrawl to convert documents into saved markdown for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Converts PDF, Word, OpenDocument, RTF, spreadsheet, and HTML files into markdown.
Saves parsed document output to a file for later review.
Generates AI summaries for supported local documents.
Answers questions about parsed document contents.
Supports markdown, HTML, and summary output formats.
Encourages incremental review of large parsed outputs.
limitations: It handles local files, not URLs.
Files are limited to 50 MB per upload.
Parsing may consume Firecrawl credits, especially for large PDFs.
Sensitive files may be processed by an external service.

use_cases.title: Review Research Papers
use_cases.description: Convert a PDF paper into markdown, then summarize findings and search important sections.

use_cases.title: Extract Operational Documents
use_cases.description: Turn manuals or spreadsheets into readable markdown for faster team review.

use_cases.title: Question Long Agreements
use_cases.description: Parse a contract and ask targeted questions about dates, terms, and obligations.

prompt_templates.title: Parse One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion for a single local document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Parse ./paper.pdf and save the markdown output in the .firecrawl folder.

prompt_templates.title: Convert and Inspect
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a converted document before deeper analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert ./docs/manual.docx to markdown, then show me the main section headings.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a concise summary from a parsed document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Parse ./research/report.pdf, create an AI summary, and save it for later review.

prompt_templates.title: Ask Targeted Questions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a long agreement or policy file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Parse ./contracts/agreement.pdf and answer these questions: What are the renewal terms, payment obligations, and termination rights?

output_examples.input: A researcher asks to parse a PDF paper and summarize the main findings.
output_examples.output: The skill saves a markdown version and returns a short summary with the central conclusions.

output_examples.input: An operations lead provides a DOCX manual and asks for the key sections.
output_examples.output: The skill produces searchable markdown and lists the main headings for review.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks specific questions about a local agreement file.
output_examples.output: The skill parses the file and gives focused answers based on the document text.

best_practices: Confirm before parsing sensitive or regulated documents.
Save large outputs to the .firecrawl folder before reading them.
Search or skim parsed output before asking broad follow-up questions.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for web URLs.
Do not stream very large parsed documents directly into the chat context.
Do not parse the same file repeatedly before checking saved output.

faq.question: What file types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports PDF, Word, OpenDocument, RTF, spreadsheet, and HTML files.

faq.question: Does it work with URLs?
faq.answer: No. Use a Firecrawl scraping skill for URLs instead.

faq.question: Where should parsed output be saved?
faq.answer: Save output in the .firecrawl folder so large files do not fill the chat context.

faq.question: Can it summarize a document?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports AI-generated summaries for parsed files.

faq.question: Can it answer questions about a file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can parse the file and answer questions based on the extracted content.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm that the file can be processed by Firecrawl and that credits are available.
